programme.name: Security & KMS Follow Along
programme.requiredOutcome: Implement a customer managed AWS KMS key with automatic rotation; encrypt and rotate a training-only Secrets Manager secret with a custom Lambda rotation function; create and inspect AWS WAF web ACL rules; enable GuardDuty and safely inspect sample threat findings; then remove all training resources, with the KMS key scheduled for deletion through AWS's required waiting period.
programme.estimatedLearnerFlow: Complete tasks in order. Infrastructure creation routes provide AWS Console steps and separate CLI verification/creation routes. When a task says a Console and CLI creation route are alternatives, create the resource once, not twice.
completionDefinition: fa-kms-admin is created for normal lab work and root is not used for day-to-day tasks.
One symmetric customer managed KMS key exists under alias/fa-kms-security-key with automatic 365-day rotation enabled.
fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret is encrypted by the customer managed KMS key.
fa-kms-rotation-function completes a training-only four-stage Secrets Manager rotation and AWSCURRENT moves to a new version.
fa-kms-web-acl contains a source-IP rate-based blocking rule plus AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet.
One GuardDuty detector is enabled in eu-west-2 and sample finding data is inspected without malicious activity.
All deletable training resources are removed in reverse dependency order.
The KMS alias is removed and the underlying customer managed key is PendingDeletion for the AWS-enforced 7-day waiting period.
Temporary IAM credentials, the CLI profile and C:\aws-labs\fa-kms are removed last.

authoringBasis.uploadedStandard: AI_Follow_Along_Steps(1).txt offline creation workflow plus the established portable offline manuscript structure used by prior Study Tracker Follow Along source files.
rulesApplied: Portable offline files only; no handoff package, session, acceptance audit or fingerprint.
Complete Console/browser and command-line routes are included where relevant.
Every important resource has an exact fa-kms name or a generated ID recorded by the learner.
All editable JSON is valid JSON; Python and shell/PowerShell content uses language text.
Only official AWS documentation is used for technical source entries.
Cleanup is manual, reverse-dependency ordered and leaves the KMS key only in AWS-required PendingDeletion.

doNotClaim: AWS or Supabase connection by the external authoring process
boundaries.destructiveSafety: Delete only exact fa-kms resources and the GuardDuty detector created by this lab. Never broaden a destructive command to unrelated resources.

warnings.cost: AWS KMS customer managed keys, AWS Secrets Manager secrets/rotation, Lambda invocations/log storage, AWS WAF web ACL/rules and GuardDuty can incur charges. Review current pricing and complete cleanup promptly. The KMS key is scheduled for deletion rather than immediately removed because AWS enforces a waiting period.
warnings.safety: Use a disposable personal training account and exact fa-kms names. The WAF web ACL is intentionally left unassociated so the lab cannot block a real application. GuardDuty uses sample findings only.
warnings.credentials: Never create root access keys. The temporary fa-kms-admin IAM-user access key is entered only through aws configure and removed after cloud cleanup. All secret values in this Follow Along are fake training values.
warnings.region: All regional resources are created in AWS eu-west-2. GuardDuty is enabled only in eu-west-2 for this lab; KMS keys and Secrets Manager secrets are Region-scoped.

tasks.title: Verify the training account, Region and local tools
tasks.goal: Confirm a disposable personal training account, eu-west-2, AWS CLI v2 and root-account safety before creating anything.
tasks.whyItMatters: Security labs can change account-wide controls, so a clean training account and known Region prevent accidental changes to unrelated resources.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 Domain 1 covers secure workloads, security services, encryption and key management.
warnings: Do not create root access keys. Root is used only for the IAM bootstrap and final training-user removal.

browserRoute.instruction: Sign in to the disposable AWS training account as the root user only long enough to confirm the account is the intended lab account.
Open the account menu and confirm the account ID is the personal training account you intend to use.
Confirm MFA is enabled for the root user. If it is not, secure the root user before continuing.
Use the Region selector and choose Europe (London), eu-west-2.
Do not create any KMS, WAF, GuardDuty, Secrets Manager or Lambda resource yet.

cliRoute.title: Verify local AWS CLI installation
cliRoute.note: No root credentials are required for this command.

expectedResults: The intended disposable training account is identified.
The working Region is eu-west-2.
AWS CLI v2 is installed locally.
No root access key exists or is created.

verificationChecks.check: Root MFA is enabled.
The Region selector shows Europe (London) eu-west-2.
aws --version returns an AWS CLI version.

troubleshooting.symptom: AWS CLI is not found
troubleshooting.fix: Install AWS CLI v2 from the official AWS CLI documentation, reopen PowerShell, and rerun aws --version.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated fa-kms IAM training user and permissions
tasks.goal: Use root only to create fa-kms-admin, attach one lab-specific customer managed policy, give it Console access, then sign out of root.
tasks.whyItMatters: Normal lab work should not run as root, and the permissions should be limited to the services and fa-kms IAM/Lambda resources used by this Follow Along.
tasks.examRelevance: IAM least privilege and separating root from normal administration are core secure-access design principles.
warnings: The policy can create IAM roles for fa-kms Lambda only; iam:PassRole is restricted to fa-kms-* roles. Never broaden it to iam:* on all resources.

browserRoute.instruction: While signed in as root, open IAM > Policies > Create policy.
Choose JSON and replace the editor contents with the complete fa-kms-admin-policy.json block supplied in this task.
Choose Next, name the policy fa-kms-admin-policy, add description Temporary permissions for the fa-kms Security and KMS Follow Along, then create the policy.
Open IAM > Users > Create user.
User name: fa-kms-admin.
Enable AWS Management Console access for this IAM user. Use an autogenerated or strong temporary password and record it outside the lab files.
On permissions, choose Attach policies directly and select only fa-kms-admin-policy.
Create the user.
Open the user and verify the Permissions tab lists fa-kms-admin-policy.
Copy the IAM sign-in URL for the account.
Sign out of root completely.
Sign in through the IAM-user sign-in URL as fa-kms-admin and confirm the console opens.
Keep the console Region set to eu-west-2.

cliRoute.title: Later verification command - do not run with root credentials
cliRoute.content:
aws iam get-user --user-name fa-kms-admin --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam list-attached-user-policies --user-name fa-kms-admin --profile fa-kms-admin
cliRoute.note: Run these only after Task 3 creates the fa-kms-admin CLI profile. A CLI creation route is intentionally not provided because it would require programmatic root credentials.

expectedResults: IAM user fa-kms-admin exists with Console access.
Customer managed policy fa-kms-admin-policy is attached.
Root is signed out before normal lab work begins.

verificationChecks.check: The Console identity is fa-kms-admin, not root.
fa-kms-admin has exactly the intended lab policy attached.
No root access key was created.

troubleshooting.symptom: Policy validation reports an action error
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the JSON with the supplied block exactly and ensure no service action name was edited.

troubleshooting.symptom: IAM user cannot sign in
troubleshooting.fix: Return to root only long enough to reset the fa-kms-admin console password or login profile, then sign out root again.

tasks.title: Create and verify the fa-kms-admin AWS CLI profile
tasks.goal: Create one temporary IAM-user access key, configure the named fa-kms-admin profile and create the dedicated local lab folder.
tasks.whyItMatters: A named profile prevents commands from silently using another account or identity and keeps all helper files inside one removable training folder.
tasks.examRelevance: Operational verification of identity and Region supports safe security administration.
warnings: Never paste the secret access key into chat, source control, JSON policies, scripts or the Follow Along files.

browserRoute.instruction: As fa-kms-admin, open IAM > Users > fa-kms-admin > Security credentials.
Under Access keys choose Create access key.
Choose Command Line Interface (CLI) as the use case, acknowledge the recommendation notice, and continue.
Create the access key and keep the access key ID and secret access key visible only long enough to enter them into aws configure.
Do not download or store the key inside C:\aws-labs\fa-kms.

cliRoute.title: Configure and verify the profile
cliRoute.content:
aws configure --profile fa-kms-admin
# Enter the temporary IAM-user access key when prompted.
# Default region name: eu-west-2
# Default output format: json

aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-kms-admin
aws configure get region --profile fa-kms-admin

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path C:\aws-labs\fa-kms -Force | Out-Null
Set-Location C:\aws-labs\fa-kms
Get-Location

expectedResults: get-caller-identity identifies the fa-kms-admin IAM user in the intended account.
The named profile region is eu-west-2.
C:\aws-labs\fa-kms exists and is the working directory.

verificationChecks.check: The returned ARN contains user/fa-kms-admin.
aws configure get region prints eu-west-2.
The current PowerShell path is C:\aws-labs\fa-kms.

troubleshooting.symptom: InvalidClientTokenId or SignatureDoesNotMatch
troubleshooting.fix: Delete the bad access key in IAM, create a new fa-kms-admin key, rerun aws configure --profile fa-kms-admin, and retest STS.

tasks.title: Create the customer managed KMS key and alias
tasks.goal: Create one symmetric encryption customer managed KMS key named by alias alias/fa-kms-security-key in eu-west-2.
tasks.whyItMatters: A customer managed key gives you control over its policy, lifecycle, aliases and rotation rather than relying only on an AWS managed key.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 expects you to choose KMS for encryption at rest and understand customer managed key control and key policies.
warnings: KMS customer managed keys can incur monthly and request charges while active.

browserRoute.instruction: Open AWS KMS in eu-west-2.
Choose Customer managed keys > Create key.
Key type: Symmetric.
Key usage: Encrypt and decrypt.
Key material origin: KMS.
Choose Next.
Alias: fa-kms-security-key. The console automatically displays it as alias/fa-kms-security-key.
Description: Security & KMS Follow Along training key.
Add tag TrainingPrefix = fa-kms.
Choose Next.
For key administrators choose fa-kms-admin.
Keep the option that allows selected key administrators to delete the key enabled for this disposable lab.
Choose Next.
For key users choose fa-kms-admin.
Review the generated key policy, then finish key creation.
Open the new key and record its Key ID in your notes; do not treat the key ID as secret.

cliRoute.title: CLI alternative - use instead of Console creation, not as well as it
cliRoute.content:
$KeyId = aws kms create-key --description "Security & KMS Follow Along training key" --key-usage ENCRYPT_DECRYPT --origin AWS_KMS --tags TagKey=TrainingPrefix,TagValue=fa-kms --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "KeyMetadata.KeyId" --output text
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/fa-kms-security-key --target-key-id $KeyId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws kms list-aliases --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "Aliases[?AliasName=='alias/fa-kms-security-key']"

expectedResults: One enabled symmetric customer managed KMS key exists in eu-west-2.
alias/fa-kms-security-key resolves to that key.
The key is tagged TrainingPrefix=fa-kms.

verificationChecks.check: Key state is Enabled.
Key usage is ENCRYPT_DECRYPT and key spec is SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT.
The alias is exactly alias/fa-kms-security-key.

troubleshooting.symptom: AccessDenied on CreateKey or CreateAlias
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm fa-kms-admin-policy is attached and the Console/CLI identity is fa-kms-admin.

troubleshooting.symptom: Alias already exists
troubleshooting.fix: Stop and confirm it is an exact resource from this lab. Do not reuse an unrelated alias.

tasks.title: Inspect the key policy and enable automatic key rotation
tasks.goal: Review how the key policy authorizes account/IAM use, then enable 365-day automatic key material rotation.
tasks.whyItMatters: KMS permissions depend on key policy as well as IAM, and key rotation changes cryptographic material without changing the key ID or alias.
tasks.examRelevance: Key policy versus IAM policy and transparent KMS key rotation are common encryption design concepts.
warnings: Do not use the bypass lockout safety option when editing a key policy.

browserRoute.instruction: Open KMS > Customer managed keys > alias/fa-kms-security-key.
Open the Key policy tab.
Identify the statement that permits the AWS account to use IAM policies for key access and the statements that identify the selected key administrator/key user.
Do not remove the account-management statement or lock yourself out.
Open the Key rotation tab.
Enable automatic key rotation.
Set the rotation period to 365 days and save.
Confirm the key details still show the same key ID and alias.

cliRoute.title: Inspect policy and enable rotation
cliRoute.content:
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --policy-name default --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --rotation-period-in-days 365 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

expectedResults: The default key policy is visible and remains manageable.
KeyRotationEnabled is true.
RotationPeriodInDays is 365.
The key ID and alias are unchanged.

verificationChecks.check: Automatic rotation is enabled.
The period is 365 days.
The key policy still allows authorized account administration.

troubleshooting.symptom: EnableKeyRotation is denied
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the key policy and fa-kms-admin IAM policy both allow the required management operation.

tasks.title: Create the KMS-encrypted Secrets Manager training secret
tasks.feature: AWS Secrets Manager with customer managed KMS key
tasks.goal: Create fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret using alias/fa-kms-security-key and a harmless training-only username/password value.
tasks.whyItMatters: Secrets Manager stores sensitive configuration separately from application code and can encrypt it with a customer managed KMS key.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 expects Secrets Manager for protected secret storage and rotation, with KMS controlling encryption at rest.
warnings: The value is fake training data. Never replace it with a real password or production secret.

browserRoute.instruction: Open Secrets Manager in eu-west-2.
Choose Store a new secret.
Secret type: Other type of secret.
Add key/value pair username = training-user.
Add key/value pair password = training-secret-v1.
Under Encryption key choose alias/fa-kms-security-key.
Choose Next.
Secret name: fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret.
Description: Training-only rotating secret for Security & KMS Follow Along.
Add tag TrainingPrefix = fa-kms.
Choose Next.
Leave automatic rotation disabled for now; it is configured after the Lambda function exists.
Finish storing the secret.
Open the secret details and confirm the Encryption key points to the fa-kms KMS key.

cliRoute.title: Create the secret from a local JSON file
cliRoute.content:
Set-Location C:\aws-labs\fa-kms
@'
{
  "username": "training-user",
  "password": "training-secret-v1"
}
'@ | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 .\fa-kms-initial-secret.json

aws secretsmanager create-secret --name fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --description "Training-only rotating secret for Security & KMS Follow Along" --kms-key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --secret-string file://fa-kms-initial-secret.json --tags Key=TrainingPrefix,Value=fa-kms --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

expectedResults: fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret exists in eu-west-2.
Its KmsKeyId identifies the customer managed fa-kms key.
Rotation is not yet enabled.

verificationChecks.check: Secret name is exactly fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret.
Encryption key is the customer managed fa-kms key.
RotationEnabled is false before the Lambda rotation setup.

troubleshooting.symptom: Secrets Manager cannot use the KMS key
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the key is Enabled and fa-kms-admin is authorized by both the KMS key policy and IAM policy.

tasks.title: Create the rotation Lambda role and complete rotation code
tasks.goal: Create fa-kms-rotation-role with limited secret/KMS access and prepare the full Python rotation function.
tasks.whyItMatters: A rotation Lambda is privileged: it must access only the intended secret and KMS key and must implement the four Secrets Manager rotation stages.
tasks.examRelevance: The exam focuses on using managed secret rotation and least privilege rather than hard-coded credentials.
warnings: This lab's setSecret and testSecret steps validate a standalone training secret only. Production rotation must update and authenticate against the real target database or service.
Never log secret values from a rotation function.

browserRoute.instruction: Open IAM > Roles > Create role.
Trusted entity type: AWS service.
Use case: Lambda.
Attach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole so the function can write operational logs.
Role name: fa-kms-rotation-role.
Create the role.
Open fa-kms-rotation-role > Permissions > Add permissions > Create inline policy.
Choose JSON and paste the complete fa-kms-rotation-role-policy.json block.
Name the inline policy fa-kms-rotation-role-policy and create it.
Confirm the role has AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole plus fa-kms-rotation-role-policy and no AdministratorAccess.

cliRoute.title: Create helper files and the rotation role
cliRoute.content:
Set-Location C:\aws-labs\fa-kms
# Save the supplied trust JSON as fa-kms-lambda-trust.json.
# Save the supplied permissions JSON as fa-kms-rotation-role-policy.json.
# Save the supplied Python as lambda_function.py.

aws iam create-role --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --assume-role-policy-document file://fa-kms-lambda-trust.json --tags Key=TrainingPrefix,Value=fa-kms --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --policy-name fa-kms-rotation-role-policy --policy-document file://fa-kms-rotation-role-policy.json --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam get-role --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam list-role-policies --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --profile fa-kms-admin

codeBlocks.title: lambda_function.py

expectedResults: fa-kms-rotation-role trusts only Lambda.
The role has basic logging and the supplied narrow secret/KMS permissions.
lambda_function.py implements createSecret, setSecret, testSecret and finishSecret.

verificationChecks.check: The role trust principal is lambda.amazonaws.com.
No AdministratorAccess policy is attached.
The inline policy secret ARN pattern is limited to fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret.
The KMS permission is constrained to alias/fa-kms-security-key.

troubleshooting.symptom: iam:PassRole warning appears in policy review
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm fa-kms-admin-policy limits PassRole to arn:aws:iam::*:role/fa-kms-* and do not broaden it.

tasks.title: Create the rotation Lambda and allow Secrets Manager to invoke it
tasks.goal: Deploy fa-kms-rotation-function, then add a resource-based permission limited to the training secret and account.
tasks.whyItMatters: Secrets Manager needs explicit permission to invoke the function, while the function separately needs an execution role for its outbound AWS API calls.
tasks.examRelevance: This separates identity-based execution-role permissions from Lambda resource-based invocation permissions.
warnings: Do not place the training secret value in Lambda environment variables or source code.

browserRoute.instruction: Open Lambda in eu-west-2 > Create function > Author from scratch.
Function name: fa-kms-rotation-function.
Runtime: Python 3.12.
Architecture: x86_64.
Under Change default execution role choose Use an existing role and select fa-kms-rotation-role.
Create the function.
Replace the default source with the complete lambda_function.py supplied in Task 7 and choose Deploy.
Open Configuration > General configuration > Edit.
Set Timeout to 30 seconds and Memory to 128 MB, then save.
Do not add VPC networking for this lab; the function uses the regional public Secrets Manager endpoint.
The Secrets Manager invocation permission is added with the CLI command below because it allows the exact source ARN and source account to be shown clearly.

cliRoute.title: Package and deploy the function
cliRoute.content:
Set-Location C:\aws-labs\fa-kms
Compress-Archive -Path .\lambda_function.py -DestinationPath .\fa-kms-rotation-function.zip -Force
$RoleArn = aws iam get-role --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --profile fa-kms-admin --query "Role.Arn" --output text
Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
aws lambda create-function --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --runtime python3.12 --handler lambda_function.lambda_handler --role $RoleArn --zip-file fileb://fa-kms-rotation-function.zip --timeout 30 --memory-size 128 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

$AccountId = aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-kms-admin --query Account --output text
$SecretArn = aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query ARN --output text
aws lambda add-permission --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --statement-id AllowSecretsManagerInvokeFaKmsSecret --action lambda:InvokeFunction --principal secretsmanager.amazonaws.com --source-account $AccountId --source-arn $SecretArn --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws lambda get-policy --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

expectedResults: fa-kms-rotation-function is Active and uses fa-kms-rotation-role.
The function timeout is 30 seconds.
Its resource policy permits secretsmanager.amazonaws.com only for the lab secret/account condition.

verificationChecks.check: Function state is Active.
Role ARN ends with role/fa-kms-rotation-role.
Lambda resource policy includes AllowSecretsManagerInvokeFaKmsSecret.

troubleshooting.symptom: CreateFunction says the role cannot be assumed
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for IAM propagation, confirm the trust principal is lambda.amazonaws.com, then retry.

troubleshooting.symptom: add-permission reports ResourceConflictException
troubleshooting.fix: Check get-policy. If the exact statement already exists, do not add a duplicate.

tasks.title: Enable rotation, rotate immediately and inspect version stages
tasks.goal: Attach fa-kms-rotation-function to the secret, set a 30-day schedule, rotate immediately and verify AWSCURRENT/AWSPREVIOUS staging without printing the password.
tasks.whyItMatters: Secrets Manager rotation creates staged versions and promotes the tested pending value to AWSCURRENT; applications should retrieve the current secret rather than hard-code a value.
tasks.examRelevance: Automated rotation reduces long-lived credentials and is a key Secrets Manager design benefit.
warnings: Do not use GetSecretValue to print the generated password. Verify rotation through metadata and version stages.

browserRoute.instruction: Open Secrets Manager > fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret > Rotation configuration > Edit rotation.
Enable Automatic rotation.
Rotation schedule: Schedule expression or interval equivalent to every 30 days.
Rotation function: fa-kms-rotation-function.
Choose Rotate immediately when the secret is stored/saved so this lab proves the workflow now.
Save the rotation configuration.
Wait until Last rotated date appears and no rotation error banner is present.
Open Versions and verify one version carries AWSCURRENT and an older version can carry AWSPREVIOUS.
Open Lambda > fa-kms-rotation-function > Monitor > View CloudWatch logs and confirm successful step messages without secret values.

cliRoute.title: Enable and verify rotation
cliRoute.content:
$RotationArn = aws lambda get-function --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "Configuration.FunctionArn" --output text
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --rotation-lambda-arn $RotationArn --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30 --rotate-immediately --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
Start-Sleep -Seconds 20
aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "{Name:Name,RotationEnabled:RotationEnabled,RotationLambdaARN:RotationLambdaARN,LastRotatedDate:LastRotatedDate,VersionIdsToStages:VersionIdsToStages}"
aws logs describe-log-streams --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-kms-rotation-function --order-by LastEventTime --descending --max-items 5 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

expectedResults: RotationEnabled is true.
RotationLambdaARN identifies fa-kms-rotation-function.
LastRotatedDate is populated.
A new AWSCURRENT version is present and the previous version is staged as AWSPREVIOUS.
The function logs contain operational success messages but no secret values.

verificationChecks.check: Rotation is enabled on a 30-day interval.
The immediate rotation completed successfully.
AWSCURRENT moved to the newly rotated version.
No password value was printed during verification.

troubleshooting.symptom: Rotation fails with AccessDeniedException
troubleshooting.fix: Inspect fa-kms-rotation-role-policy, the KMS alias condition, and the Lambda resource policy. Correct only the missing fa-kms permission and retry.

troubleshooting.symptom: Rotation fails in setSecret or testSecret
troubleshooting.fix: Open the Lambda logs and verify the complete training code was deployed. Do not log or print the secret value.

tasks.title: Create the regional WAF web ACL with two protection rules
tasks.goal: Create fa-kms-web-acl with default Allow, an IP rate-based Block rule and AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet.
tasks.whyItMatters: WAF evaluates ordered Layer 7 rules before the default action, and managed rule groups reduce the amount of custom attack-pattern logic you must maintain.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 explicitly includes WAF as an application security control and expects you to distinguish it from network firewalls and DDoS services.
warnings: AWS WAF web ACLs and rules can incur charges even when this training ACL is not associated with an application resource.

browserRoute.instruction: Open AWS WAF & Shield in eu-west-2.
Choose Web ACLs > Create web ACL.
Name: fa-kms-web-acl.
Resource type/Region: Regional resources, Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Do not associate a production or unrelated resource. This lab intentionally proves the web ACL configuration without attaching it to an application.
Default web ACL action: Allow.
Add rule > Add my own rules and rule groups > Rule builder.
Rule type: Rate-based rule.
Name: fa-kms-rate-limit.
Rate limit: 100 requests for the default five-minute evaluation window.
Request aggregation: Source IP address.
Action: Block.
Add the rule.
Add rules > Add managed rule groups > AWS managed rule groups.
Add Core rule set (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet).
Keep its normal managed actions and name/reference it as fa-kms-common-rules where the console permits the rule reference name.
Set priority so fa-kms-rate-limit is evaluated before the managed rule group.
Enable sampled requests and CloudWatch metrics for the web ACL/rules.
Create the web ACL.

cliRoute.title: Create the web ACL from complete JSON
cliRoute.content:
Set-Location C:\aws-labs\fa-kms
# Save the supplied JSON block as fa-kms-web-acl.json.
aws wafv2 create-web-acl --cli-input-json file://fa-kms-web-acl.json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "WebACLs[?Name=='fa-kms-web-acl']"

codeBlocks.title: fa-kms-web-acl.json

expectedResults: fa-kms-web-acl exists with REGIONAL scope in eu-west-2.
Default action is Allow.
Priority 0 is fa-kms-rate-limit with Block action and IP aggregation.
Priority 1 references AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet.
CloudWatch metrics and sampled requests are enabled.

verificationChecks.check: The web ACL scope is REGIONAL.
Exactly the two intended rules are present.
The rate limit is 100 and aggregate key type is IP.
No application resource is associated with this training web ACL.

troubleshooting.symptom: WAF rejects the JSON
troubleshooting.fix: Replace the local file with the complete supplied fa-kms-web-acl.json and retry without editing property names.

troubleshooting.symptom: Managed rule group name is rejected
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm VendorName is AWS and Name is AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet.

tasks.title: Review WAF rule order, visibility and rate-limit behavior
tasks.goal: Inspect the created web ACL and explain what would happen to requests as each rule and the default action are evaluated.
tasks.whyItMatters: Rule priority and terminating actions decide which controls can see a request; understanding this is more important than memorizing the console screens.
tasks.examRelevance: A solutions architect must choose appropriate request filtering and rate limiting at the application edge or regional web layer.
warnings: Because the web ACL is deliberately unassociated, there are no real request samples or rate-limited IPs in this lab.

browserRoute.instruction: Open WAF > Web ACLs > fa-kms-web-acl > Rules.
Confirm fa-kms-rate-limit has the lower priority number and therefore runs first.
Open the rate rule and confirm it groups request counts by source IP and blocks after the configured threshold.
Open fa-kms-common-rules and identify that it is an AWS managed rule group rather than a hand-written pattern list.
Open the Overview/Traffic sections and confirm metrics/sampled requests are enabled, while recognizing there will be no traffic because no resource is associated.
Confirm the default action is Allow for requests that no rule blocks.

cliRoute.title: Retrieve the complete web ACL
cliRoute.content:
$AclId = aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "WebACLs[?Name=='fa-kms-web-acl'].Id | [0]" --output text
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name fa-kms-web-acl --scope REGIONAL --id $AclId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "WebACL.{DefaultAction:DefaultAction,Rules:Rules,VisibilityConfig:VisibilityConfig}"

expectedResults: The retrieved configuration shows priority 0 rate blocking followed by priority 1 common managed rules.
The default action remains Allow.
No protected resource association exists.

verificationChecks.check: You can state that lower numeric priority is evaluated first.
You can state that the rate rule tracks counts per source IP.
You can distinguish managed rule groups from custom rules.

troubleshooting.symptom: get-web-acl requires an ID
troubleshooting.fix: Run the list-web-acls command first and use the ID returned for fa-kms-web-acl.

tasks.title: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in eu-west-2
tasks.goal: Create and enable one GuardDuty detector in eu-west-2 and record its generated detector ID.
tasks.whyItMatters: GuardDuty continuously analyzes supported AWS data sources and emits security findings without requiring you to deploy monitoring servers.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 Domain 1 names GuardDuty as a security service for threat detection use cases.
warnings: GuardDuty can incur usage charges after any applicable trial. Keep this lab in eu-west-2 only and disable the detector during cleanup.

browserRoute.instruction: Open Amazon GuardDuty and confirm the Region is eu-west-2.
If GuardDuty is already enabled from unrelated work, stop rather than modifying that existing detector; this Follow Along assumes a clean training account.
Choose Get Started or Enable GuardDuty.
Review the enablement page and enable GuardDuty for this Region.
Do not opt into unrelated paid protection-plan experiments for this lab.
Open Settings and record the Detector ID shown for eu-west-2.
Open Summary and Findings and confirm the service is enabled even if no real findings exist.

cliRoute.title: CLI alternative - create and verify the detector
cliRoute.content:
$DetectorId = aws guardduty create-detector --enable --finding-publishing-frequency FIFTEEN_MINUTES --tags TrainingPrefix=fa-kms --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query DetectorId --output text
$DetectorId
aws guardduty get-detector --detector-id $DetectorId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

expectedResults: One GuardDuty detector exists and is enabled in eu-west-2.
A detector ID is available for later sample-finding and cleanup commands.

verificationChecks.check: Detector Status is ENABLED.
The detector is in eu-west-2 only for this lab.
The detector ID has been recorded.

troubleshooting.symptom: create-detector says GuardDuty is already enabled
troubleshooting.fix: Do not create or alter a second detector. Confirm whether the existing detector belongs to this lab; if not, stop this task to avoid changing unrelated security monitoring.

tasks.title: Generate and inspect a safe GuardDuty sample finding
tasks.goal: Generate sample finding data without performing malicious activity, then inspect finding type, severity and affected resource fields.
tasks.whyItMatters: Sample findings let you learn the finding structure and test downstream handling without attacking or compromising a real resource.
tasks.examRelevance: GuardDuty findings identify suspicious activity; architects should know GuardDuty detects and reports rather than directly blocking every threat.
warnings: Use generated sample findings only; do not create real malicious traffic or attack simulations in this lab.

browserRoute.instruction: Open GuardDuty > Settings.
Find Sample findings and choose Generate sample findings.
Open Findings.
Filter or visually identify findings whose titles start with [SAMPLE].
Open one sample finding.
Review Severity, Finding type, Resource affected and Action/Actor details.
Confirm the record is clearly marked as a sample.
Do not treat the sample as a real incident.

cliRoute.title: Generate one documented sample finding and inspect it
cliRoute.content:
$DetectorId = aws guardduty list-detectors --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "DetectorIds[0]" --output text
aws guardduty create-sample-findings --detector-id $DetectorId --finding-types Backdoor:EC2/DenialOfService.Tcp --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
$FindingId = aws guardduty list-findings --detector-id $DetectorId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "FindingIds[0]" --output text
aws guardduty get-findings --detector-id $DetectorId --finding-ids $FindingId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "Findings[0].{Title:Title,Type:Type,Severity:Severity,Resource:Resource.ResourceType,Sample:Service.AdditionalInfo}"

expectedResults: At least one [SAMPLE] finding appears.
The finding has a type, severity and resource description.
No real malicious workload was created.

verificationChecks.check: The inspected finding is explicitly a sample.
You can identify its severity and finding type.
You can explain that GuardDuty detects and reports suspicious behavior rather than acting as WAF.

troubleshooting.symptom: No sample appears immediately
troubleshooting.fix: Refresh Findings after a short interval and confirm the detector is still ENABLED in eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Review the security architecture and SAA-C03 decision points
tasks.goal: Connect KMS, Secrets Manager, WAF and GuardDuty to the problem each service solves and identify common exam traps.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam tests service selection and boundaries more often than button-by-button creation steps.
tasks.examRelevance: This task directly consolidates SAA-C03 Domain 1 secure architecture choices.

browserRoute.instruction: Open KMS and confirm the customer managed key controls encryption and key lifecycle rather than storing the application secret itself.
Open Secrets Manager and confirm the secret uses the fa-kms KMS key and has automatic rotation enabled.
Open WAF and confirm it evaluates web request rules; it is not a replacement for IAM, security groups or GuardDuty.
Open GuardDuty and confirm it produces threat findings; it is not a web request firewall.
Review these exam distinctions: KMS manages encryption keys; Secrets Manager stores/rotates secrets; WAF filters supported Layer 7 web traffic; GuardDuty detects suspicious activity.
Review the key-policy trap: an IAM Allow alone may not be enough if the KMS key policy does not permit the access path.
Review the rotation trap: KMS key rotation changes backing key material transparently, while Secrets Manager rotation changes the secret value and often updates a target service.

cliRoute.title: Run a final non-destructive inventory
cliRoute.content:
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "KeyMetadata.{KeyId:KeyId,KeyState:KeyState,KeyManager:KeyManager}"
aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "{Name:Name,RotationEnabled:RotationEnabled,KmsKeyId:KmsKeyId}"
aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "WebACLs[?Name=='fa-kms-web-acl']"
aws guardduty list-detectors --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

expectedResults: All four service areas are present and their responsibilities can be explained correctly.
The inventory shows only the intended fa-kms training resources plus the generated GuardDuty detector ID.

verificationChecks.check: You can explain KMS versus Secrets Manager.
You can explain WAF versus GuardDuty.
You can explain KMS key-material rotation versus secret-value rotation.
No cleanup has started yet.

tasks.title: Remove WAF, GuardDuty, Secrets Manager, Lambda and KMS resources safely
tasks.goal: Delete or schedule deletion of every cloud resource created by the lab, keeping the IAM training identity until cloud verification is complete.
tasks.whyItMatters: Security resources can continue to incur cost or retain sensitive configuration if cleanup stops early, and KMS keys require a waiting period before final deletion.
tasks.examRelevance: Safe lifecycle control and dependency-aware deletion are operational security practices.
warnings: These commands are destructive. Delete only exact fa-kms resources.
The KMS key cannot be deleted immediately; schedule it for the minimum 7-day waiting period and verify PendingDeletion.

browserRoute.instruction: WAF: open fa-kms-web-acl and confirm it has no associated resource, then delete exactly fa-kms-web-acl.
GuardDuty: in eu-west-2 open Settings and disable GuardDuty for this Region. Understand that disabling removes the detector configuration and findings for the Region.
Secrets Manager: open fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret and delete this fake training secret. Choose the lab's immediate/force-delete path only because the value is disposable and the name is exact.
Lambda: delete fa-kms-rotation-function.
CloudWatch Logs: delete /aws/lambda/fa-kms-rotation-function if the rotation invocation created it.
IAM role: detach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole from fa-kms-rotation-role, delete inline policy fa-kms-rotation-role-policy, then delete fa-kms-rotation-role.
KMS: open alias/fa-kms-security-key and note the Key ID before deleting the alias.
Delete alias alias/fa-kms-security-key.
Schedule the underlying customer managed KMS key for deletion with a 7-day waiting period.
Verify the key state is Pending deletion/PendingDeletion and record the deletion date.
Do not delete fa-kms-admin yet; it is needed for command-line verification.

cliRoute.title: Delete cloud resources in safe order
cliRoute.content:
$AclId = aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "WebACLs[?Name=='fa-kms-web-acl'].Id | [0]" --output text
$LockToken = aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name fa-kms-web-acl --scope REGIONAL --id $AclId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query LockToken --output text
aws wafv2 delete-web-acl --name fa-kms-web-acl --scope REGIONAL --id $AclId --lock-token $LockToken --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

$DetectorId = aws guardduty list-detectors --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "DetectorIds[0]" --output text
aws guardduty delete-detector --detector-id $DetectorId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --force-delete-without-recovery --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

aws lambda delete-function --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws logs delete-log-group --log-group-name /aws/lambda/fa-kms-rotation-function --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin

aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --policy-name fa-kms-rotation-role-policy --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam delete-role --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --profile fa-kms-admin

$KeyId = aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/fa-kms-security-key --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "KeyMetadata.KeyId" --output text
aws kms delete-alias --alias-name alias/fa-kms-security-key --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id $KeyId --pending-window-in-days 7 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws kms describe-key --key-id $KeyId --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "KeyMetadata.{KeyId:KeyId,KeyState:KeyState,DeletionDate:DeletionDate}"

cliRoute.title: Verify cloud resources are removed or pending deletion
cliRoute.content:
aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin --query "WebACLs[?Name=='fa-kms-web-acl']"
aws guardduty list-detectors --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws lambda get-function --function-name fa-kms-rotation-function --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-kms-admin
aws iam get-role --role-name fa-kms-rotation-role --profile fa-kms-admin
cliRoute.note: Expected: WAF list is empty for the named ACL; GuardDuty list is empty; Secrets Manager reports scheduled deletion/not found; Lambda and IAM role return ResourceNotFound/NoSuchEntity; KMS reports PendingDeletion by Key ID.

expectedResults: fa-kms-web-acl is deleted.
GuardDuty detector is deleted/disabled in eu-west-2.
fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret is force-deleted/scheduled for asynchronous immediate deletion.
fa-kms-rotation-function and its log group are absent.
fa-kms-rotation-role is absent.
alias/fa-kms-security-key is absent.
The underlying KMS key is PendingDeletion with a 7-day waiting period.

verificationChecks.check: No fa-kms WAF web ACL remains.
No GuardDuty detector remains in eu-west-2 from this lab.
The training secret cannot be used.
The Lambda function and role are absent.
The KMS alias is absent and the key is PendingDeletion.

troubleshooting.symptom: WAF deletion reports a stale lock token
troubleshooting.fix: Run get-web-acl again to obtain the latest LockToken and retry the exact delete.

troubleshooting.symptom: KMS key cannot be scheduled for deletion
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the secret and alias are removed, the key is Enabled, and you are targeting the exact Key ID recorded from alias/fa-kms-security-key.

troubleshooting.symptom: CloudWatch log group does not exist
troubleshooting.fix: That is acceptable if no log group was created; continue only after confirming the Lambda function itself is deleted.

tasks.title: Remove the training access key, IAM user, policy, CLI profile and local files
tasks.goal: Remove temporary credentials only after cloud cleanup is verified, then delete the exact local lab folder and acknowledge completion.
tasks.whyItMatters: Deleting credentials too early can strand chargeable resources, while leaving credentials after the lab creates unnecessary account risk.
tasks.examRelevance: Credential lifecycle and least privilege include removing temporary access after use.
warnings: Root is used only for final removal of the temporary IAM user/policy; sign out again immediately afterward.

browserRoute.instruction: While still signed in as fa-kms-admin, open IAM > Users > fa-kms-admin > Security credentials.
Delete the temporary access key only after Task 15 cloud verification is complete.
Sign out of fa-kms-admin.
Sign in as root for final IAM cleanup only.
Open IAM > Users > fa-kms-admin and delete the user after confirming it owns no remaining lab role or cloud resource.
Open IAM > Policies, select fa-kms-admin-policy and delete the customer managed policy.
Confirm fa-kms-admin and fa-kms-admin-policy are absent.
Sign out of root.
Delete the local AWS CLI profile and the exact C:\aws-labs\fa-kms folder using the CLI/local commands below.
Do not delete C:\aws-labs or any sibling lab folder.

cliRoute.title: Remove the named CLI profile and local helper files
cliRoute.content:
aws configure unset aws_access_key_id --profile fa-kms-admin
aws configure unset aws_secret_access_key --profile fa-kms-admin
aws configure unset region --profile fa-kms-admin
aws configure unset output --profile fa-kms-admin

if (Test-Path "C:\aws-labs\fa-kms") {
  Remove-Item "C:\aws-labs\fa-kms" -Recurse -Force
}
Test-Path "C:\aws-labs\fa-kms"
cliRoute.note: Run this after the IAM access key has been deleted. Test-Path should return False.

expectedResults: The temporary IAM access key is deleted.
fa-kms-admin and fa-kms-admin-policy are deleted by root.
The fa-kms-admin named CLI profile no longer contains credentials/Region/output.
C:\aws-labs\fa-kms is absent.
Only the AWS-enforced PendingDeletion KMS key remains until its deletion date.

verificationChecks.check: fa-kms-admin no longer exists.
fa-kms-admin-policy no longer exists.
The named CLI profile no longer contains usable credentials.
C:\aws-labs\fa-kms returns False from Test-Path.
The final cleanup acknowledgement can be made truthfully.

troubleshooting.symptom: IAM user deletion says resources or credentials remain
troubleshooting.fix: Remove only the fa-kms-admin access key/login profile/policy attachment shown by IAM, then retry. Do not alter unrelated users.

troubleshooting.symptom: AccessDenied after switching from root to fa-kms-admin
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the exact fa-kms-admin-policy is attached and aws sts get-caller-identity or the Console identity shows fa-kms-admin.

troubleshooting.symptom: A KMS action is allowed in IAM but still denied
troubleshooting.fix: Inspect the KMS key policy as well as IAM. KMS authorization can require both the key policy access path and identity permission.

troubleshooting.symptom: Secrets Manager rotation fails
troubleshooting.fix: Inspect Lambda logs, the execution-role secret/KMS permissions and Lambda's Secrets Manager invocation resource policy; never print the secret to troubleshoot.

troubleshooting.symptom: WAF web ACL cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm it has no association and retrieve a fresh LockToken before delete-web-acl.

troubleshooting.symptom: GuardDuty sample findings do not appear
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the detector is ENABLED in eu-west-2 and refresh after generating samples.

troubleshooting.symptom: KMS key still exists after cleanup
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected during the 7-day PendingDeletion window. Verify the alias is deleted and KeyState is PendingDeletion.

steps.action: Delete the unassociated REGIONAL WAF web ACL using the latest lock token.

steps.resource: GuardDuty detector created for the lab in eu-west-2
steps.action: Delete the detector to disable GuardDuty in the Region.
Force-delete only the fake training secret after rotation is complete.
steps.verification: The secret is scheduled for immediate asynchronous deletion or is no longer found.

steps.action: Delete the Lambda function, then delete its log group if present.
steps.verification: Lambda get-function fails for the name and the log group is absent.

steps.action: Detach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, delete fa-kms-rotation-role-policy, then delete the role.
Record the Key ID, delete the alias, then schedule the underlying KMS key for deletion with a 7-day waiting period.
steps.verification: Alias is absent and describe-key by Key ID reports PendingDeletion plus DeletionDate.

steps.action: Delete the access key only after cloud cleanup verification.
steps.verification: No active access key remains for fa-kms-admin.

steps.action: Use root only to delete the temporary training user and its customer managed policy, then sign out root.
steps.verification: IAM shows neither the user nor policy.

steps.action: Unset the exact profile credentials, Region and output configuration.
steps.verification: The named profile contains no usable credentials.

steps.action: Delete the exact local lab folder last.

cleanup.programmeCleanupAcknowledgement: I verified that fa-kms-web-acl is deleted; the lab GuardDuty detector is disabled/deleted in eu-west-2; fa-kms-rotating-demo-secret is deleted or in its immediate asynchronous deletion process; fa-kms-rotation-function, its CloudWatch log group and fa-kms-rotation-role are absent; alias/fa-kms-security-key is deleted and its exact underlying customer managed key is PendingDeletion with a recorded deletion date; the temporary fa-kms-admin access key, IAM user and fa-kms-admin-policy are removed; the fa-kms-admin CLI profile contains no usable credentials; and only then was C:\aws-labs\fa-kms deleted.

conversionNotesForLocalCodex: Preserve programme title, ID, learner level, exam workspace, Region and fa-kms resource prefix.
Do not turn the training-only standalone secret rotation function into a claim that a real database credential was rotated.
Do not add a WAF resource association; the unassociated web ACL is intentional for safety and cost containment.
Do not convert PendingDeletion into a claim that the KMS key has already been physically deleted.
